div.div: Re-composed from Workbook Module 1 for web readability

Regional specialty distributors whose operations teams are outgrowing manual handoffs between sales, order/inventory, and accounting systems, where Casey's integration and workflow-application capability may reduce fragmentation without requiring a full system replacement.
Why this deserves focused attention now

The context is recognizable and sourceable. Casey's real capability fits. Relevant technical proof exists. There is a plausible route to buyer and partner evidence. Paid professional integration work is commercially plausible without inventing market-size or ROI claims.
Past integration/workflow experience, agency and professional relationships, technical artifacts, observed operational workflow problems from prior work.
Buying-situation frequency, buyer role, buyer language, dominant consequences, alternatives, proof requirements, budget path, and strongest market-access route.

Revise if the first buyer-research cycle fails to uncover credible buying situations, if the market proves practically unreachable, if evidence points to a different problem or market, or if another hypothesis develops materially stronger evidence and access.
